uncited: Acceleration techniques in volume rendering reduce the computational cost of generating images by minimizing redundant sampling, skipping invisible data, or parallelizing work.
This family solves the bottleneck of evaluating the volume rendering integral for every ray or voxel, which is often prohibitively expensive for high-resolution datasets or neural fields.

Unlike [Image-order rendering](16-image-order-rendering.md) which defines the traversal order (eye-space), acceleration methods optimize the *content* of that traversal—whether by skipping empty space, terminating rays early, or adapting resolution—without changing the fundamental image-order nature of the parent.
The core mechanism shared by all acceleration methods is the reduction of work units (samples, voxels, or pixels) processed per frame while maintaining acceptable visual fidelity.
